observations: The architectures were locked before Fashion-MNIST evaluation; no architecture search was performed on the new dataset.
h64_512 achieved mean Q.ANT accuracy 0.85867 with 88650 parameters, versus h128 at 0.85040 with 101770 parameters.
h128_512 achieved 0.85913 with 171658 parameters, essentially matching h256 at 0.85923 while using fewer parameters.
The Pareto front is h64_512, h128_512, h256, h512; h128 is not Pareto-efficient.
h512 retained the highest mean accuracy at 0.86493 but uses 407050 parameters.
Q.ANT CPU and PyTorch predictions differed on 5-18 of 10000 test examples per run.
interpretation: The parameter-efficiency pattern transfers beyond MNIST: the fixed h64_512 architecture clearly outperforms h128 with fewer parameters, while h128_512 nearly matches h256 with fewer parameters. However, the evidence does not show universal dominance of bottleneck-plus-expansion architectures because h256 and h512 remain Pareto-efficient. This supports cross-dataset generalization of a parameter-efficiency effect, with qualification.
limitations: Fashion-MNIST is still a small 28x28 grayscale benchmark closely matched in shape to MNIST.
Only three seeds and three epochs were used.
The Q.ANT CPU backend does not measure photonic latency, energy efficiency, throughput, or optical behavior.
next_research_direction: Move from generic ReLU dense topology comparisons toward a Q.ANT-specific architectural hypothesis, such as testing supported nonlinear or KAN-style operations under controlled parameter budgets, before eventual validation on real photonic hardware.
